---- MODULE W4Od0m4p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Patient, MaxQueue, NoPatient

\* Backpressure: the waiting queue may never grow past MaxQueue.
\* Irreversibility: a patient may be appended to the completed-surgery
\* log (history) at most once -- AdmitPatient refuses anyone already logged.

VARIABLES queue, inOR, history, crashed, backupActive

vars == <<queue, inOR, history, crashed, backupActive>>

RangeSeq(s) == { s[i] : i \in 1..Len(s) }

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \in Seq(Patient)
  /\ Len(queue) <= MaxQueue
  /\ inOR \in Patient \cup {NoPatient}
  /\ history \in Seq(Patient)
  /\ crashed \in BOOLEAN
  /\ backupActive \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ inOR = NoPatient
  /\ history = <<>>
  /\ crashed = FALSE
  /\ backupActive = FALSE

Available == ~crashed \/ backupActive

AdmitPatient(p) ==
  /\ Len(queue) < MaxQueue
  /\ p \notin RangeSeq(queue)
  /\ p \notin RangeSeq(history)
  /\ inOR # p
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, p)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inOR, history, crashed, backupActive>>

BeginSurgery ==
  /\ inOR = NoPatient
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ Available
  /\ inOR' = Head(queue)
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<history, crashed, backupActive>>

FinishSurgery ==
  /\ inOR # NoPatient
  /\ history' = Append(history, inOR)
  /\ inOR' = NoPatient
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, crashed, backupActive>>

SurgeonCrashes ==
  /\ ~crashed
  /\ crashed' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inOR, history, backupActive>>

ActivateBackup ==
  /\ crashed
  /\ ~backupActive
  /\ backupActive' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inOR, history, crashed>>

\* The primary surgeon can also silently return to duty once the OR and the
\* queue are both empty (i.e. only between cases, never abandoning a patient
\* mid-flight); this keeps at least one staffing action always available so
\* the model never wedges once every admitted patient has been treated.
SurgeonRecovers ==
  /\ crashed
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ inOR = NoPatient
  /\ crashed' = FALSE
  /\ backupActive' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inOR, history>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Patient : AdmitPatient(p)
  \/ BeginSurgery
  \/ FinishSurgery
  \/ SurgeonCrashes
  \/ ActivateBackup
  \/ SurgeonRecovers

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(BeginSurgery)
  /\ WF_vars(FinishSurgery)
  /\ WF_vars(ActivateBackup)

\* SAFETY: no patient's surgery is ever recorded twice in the log.
NoRepeatSurgery ==
  \A i, j \in 1..Len(history) : i # j => history[i] # history[j]

InQueueOrOR(p) == p \in RangeSeq(queue) \/ inOR = p
InHistory(p) == p \in RangeSeq(history)

\* LIVENESS: any patient waiting or in the OR is eventually logged as done.
EventualTreatment == \A p \in Patient : InQueueOrOR(p) ~> InHistory(p)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Patient = {p1, p2, p3}
  MaxQueue = 2
  NoPatient = NoPatient

INVARIANT NoRepeatSurgery
PROPERTY EventualTreatment
nl:
This spec models a hospital operating-room (OR) scheduler. Patients are admitted into a
bounded waiting queue; the queue has a fixed capacity and admission is refused once it is
full (backpressure), so the hospital never over-promises OR time to more patients than it
can track. A single OR takes the next patient from the front of the queue and begins their
procedure. When the procedure finishes, the patient's surgery is permanently recorded in the
hospital's completed-surgery log and the OR becomes free for the next case. The primary
surgeon staffing the OR can, without any warning event, become unavailable (crash silently)
partway through the day; while the surgeon is marked unavailable no new procedure can begin.
A backup surgeon can be activated by the charge nurse once the primary is found unavailable,
after which cases resume moving through the OR exactly as before. The full action set is:
AdmitPatient (append a patient to the waiting queue, refused when the queue is at capacity or
the patient has already been treated), BeginSurgery (pull the head of the queue into the OR,
only possible when the OR is empty and some surgeon -- primary or backup -- is available),
FinishSurgery (append the patient currently in the OR to the completed-surgery log and empty
the OR), SurgeonCrashes (the primary surgeon silently becomes unavailable, an event that is never
announced), ActivateBackup (the charge nurse brings the backup surgeon online once the
primary has crashed), and SurgeonRecovers (the primary silently returns to duty and the backup is stood down,
but only in a lull when the queue and OR are both empty, never abandoning a patient
mid-case, so staffing can cycle for as long as the hospital stays open).
SAFETY PROPERTY: no patient's name is ever recorded twice in the completed-surgery log, i.e. every patient's surgery is completed at most once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every patient who is waiting in the queue or currently in the OR is eventually recorded in the completed-surgery log, even if the primary surgeon silently crashes.

---- MODULE W4Od3m9p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS BatchIds, MaxEpoch, MaxCapacity, MaxPending

\* Epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the clearing house cycles through epochs,
\* and each new epoch is free to pick a different settlement capacity at
\* runtime. Settlement itself is irreversible: once a batch id is in
\* `settled` it can never return to `pending`, so a batch clears at most once.

VARIABLES epoch, capacity, settledThisEpoch, pending, settled

vars == <<epoch, capacity, settledThisEpoch, pending, settled>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCapacity
  /\ settledThisEpoch \in 0..MaxCapacity
  /\ pending \subseteq BatchIds
  /\ settled \subseteq BatchIds

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ capacity = 1
  /\ settledThisEpoch = 0
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ settled = {}

SubmitBatch(b) ==
  /\ b \notin pending
  /\ b \notin settled
  /\ Cardinality(pending) < MaxPending
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, settledThisEpoch, settled>>

SettleBatch(b) ==
  /\ b \in pending
  /\ settledThisEpoch < capacity
  /\ pending' = pending \ {b}
  /\ settled' = settled \cup {b}
  /\ settledThisEpoch' = settledThisEpoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity>>

CancelPending(b) ==
  /\ b \in pending
  /\ pending' = pending \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, settledThisEpoch, settled>>

\* The epoch counter wraps rather than growing unboundedly, and capacity is
\* re-picked independently each time, so reconfiguration is always available
\* -- it is never disabled just because a prior epoch used up its capacity.
Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch' = (epoch + 1) % (MaxEpoch + 1)
  /\ capacity' \in 1..MaxCapacity
  /\ settledThisEpoch' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, settled>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in BatchIds : SubmitBatch(b)
  \/ \E b \in BatchIds : SettleBatch(b)
  \/ \E b \in BatchIds : CancelPending(b)
  \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: settlement is a one-way step -- a settled batch id never reappears
\* in the pending set (no replay/undo of an already-final settlement).
SettlementCoherence == pending \cap settled = {}

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  BatchIds = {b1, b2, b3}
  MaxEpoch = 3
  MaxCapacity = 2
  MaxPending = 2

INVARIANT SettlementCoherence
nl:
This spec models an interbank settlement batch process organized into numbered epochs. Each
epoch has its own settlement capacity -- the maximum number of interbank transfers that may be
finally settled inside that epoch -- and a reconfiguration step at the epoch boundary is free
to raise or lower that capacity to match current liquidity and risk limits, so the capacity is
not fixed once and for all but changes at runtime as epochs roll forward. A batch (identified
by a batch id) moves through three states: it is submitted for settlement, it may sit pending
while capacity is unavailable, and once actually settled it is done forever -- settlement is
the irreversible step that finally moves money between the two banks and can never be replayed
or undone for that batch id, and a bank may not resubmit a batch id that has already settled.
The full action set is: SubmitBatch (a bank places a not-yet-seen, not-yet-settled batch id
into the pending set), SettleBatch (the clearing house finally settles one pending batch id,
consuming one unit of the current epoch's remaining settlement capacity), CancelPending (a
bank withdraws one of its own batch ids from the pending set before it is settled, e.g.
because the counterparty backed out), and Reconfigure (the clearing house advances to the next
epoch, resets the count of batches settled so far this epoch to zero, and picks a fresh
capacity for the new epoch, independent of the capacity that came before).
SAFETY PROPERTY: a batch id that has already been finally settled can never simultaneously sit in the pending set, i.e. settlement is a one-way, non-replayable step for every batch id.

---- MODULE W4Od2m8p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, NumZones, SlotsPerZone, NoRobot

\* Hierarchical locking: a robot must take the coarse zone lock covering its
\* target slot before it may take the fine-grained slot lock; the zone lock
\* is released again as soon as the slot itself is held, since it was only
\* ever needed to arbitrate entry into the zone.

Zones == 1..NumZones
Slots == 1..(NumZones * SlotsPerZone)
ZoneOf(s) == ((s - 1) \div SlotsPerZone) + 1

VARIABLES phase, target, zoneLock, slotOwner

vars == <<phase, target, zoneLock, slotOwner>>

Phases == {"idle", "wantZone", "wantSlot", "holding"}

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in [Robots -> Phases]
  /\ target \in [Robots -> Slots]
  /\ zoneLock \in [Zones -> Robots \cup {NoRobot}]
  /\ slotOwner \in [Slots -> Robots \cup {NoRobot}]

Init ==
  /\ phase = [r \in Robots |-> "idle"]
  /\ target \in [Robots -> Slots]
  /\ zoneLock = [z \in Zones |-> NoRobot]
  /\ slotOwner = [s \in Slots |-> NoRobot]

RequestSlot(r) ==
  /\ phase[r] = "idle"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "wantZone"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, zoneLock, slotOwner>>

AcquireZoneLock(r) ==
  /\ phase[r] = "wantZone"
  /\ zoneLock[ZoneOf(target[r])] = NoRobot
  /\ zoneLock' = [zoneLock EXCEPT ![ZoneOf(target[r])] = r]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "wantSlot"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, slotOwner>>

AcquireSlot(r) ==
  /\ phase[r] = "wantSlot"
  /\ zoneLock[ZoneOf(target[r])] = r
  /\ slotOwner[target[r]] = NoRobot
  /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![target[r]] = r]
  /\ zoneLock' = [zoneLock EXCEPT ![ZoneOf(target[r])] = NoRobot]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "holding"]
  /\ UNCHANGED target

ReleaseSlot(r) ==
  /\ phase[r] = "holding"
  /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![target[r]] = NoRobot]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, zoneLock>>

\* Privileged admin override #1: reclaim a held slot without the robot's
\* cooperation (e.g. to redirect stock during an emergency).
AdminForceRelease(s) ==
  /\ slotOwner[s] # NoRobot
  /\ LET r == slotOwner[s] IN
       /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = NoRobot]
       /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<target, zoneLock>>

\* Privileged admin override #2: redirect an idle robot's designated slot
\* before it begins its locking sequence.
AdminReassignTarget(r, s) ==
  /\ phase[r] = "idle"
  /\ target[r] # s
  /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![r] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, zoneLock, slotOwner>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Robots : RequestSlot(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : AcquireZoneLock(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : AcquireSlot(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : ReleaseSlot(r)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : AdminForceRelease(s)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, s \in Slots : AdminReassignTarget(r, s)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A r \in Robots : WF_vars(RequestSlot(r))
  /\ \A r \in Robots : SF_vars(AcquireZoneLock(r))
  /\ \A r \in Robots : SF_vars(AcquireSlot(r))
  /\ \A r \in Robots : WF_vars(ReleaseSlot(r))

\* SAFETY: no two robots ever simultaneously hold the same slot.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A r1, r2 \in Robots :
    (r1 # r2 /\ phase[r1] = "holding" /\ phase[r2] = "holding") => target[r1] # target[r2]

\* LIVENESS: every robot that starts wanting a slot eventually holds it.
EventualHolding == \A r \in Robots : (phase[r] = "wantZone") ~> (phase[r] = "holding")

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Robots = {r1, r2}
  NumZones = 2
  SlotsPerZone = 2
  NoRobot = NoRobot

INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
PROPERTY EventualHolding
nl:
This spec models a warehouse robot fleet that uses hierarchical locking to reserve storage
slots. The warehouse floor is divided into zones, and each zone contains several storage
slots. Before a robot may claim a specific slot for an item, it must first take the coarse
zone lock for the zone that slot lives in, and only afterward take the fine-grained slot lock
itself; once the slot lock is granted the zone lock is released again, since the coarse lock
was only ever needed to arbitrate entry into the zone, not to hold the slot long-term. A
privileged warehouse admin can, at any time, forcibly reclaim a slot a robot is currently
holding (for example to redirect stock during an emergency) and can also redirect an idle
robot to a different target slot before it starts its locking sequence. The full action set
is: RequestSlot (an idle robot picks its designated target slot and starts wanting the
enclosing zone's coarse lock), AcquireZoneLock (the robot takes the free coarse zone lock for
the zone containing its target slot), AcquireSlot (holding the zone lock, the robot claims its
target slot itself, becomes its holder, and immediately releases the coarse zone lock),
ReleaseSlot (a holding robot finishes its work and gives the slot back up, becoming idle
again), AdminForceRelease (the admin strips slot ownership from whichever robot holds a given
slot, without that robot's cooperation), and AdminReassignTarget (the admin changes an idle
robot's designated target slot before it begins locking).
SAFETY PROPERTY: no two robots ever simultaneously believe they are the holder of the same storage slot, i.e. a slot is never double-allocated.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every robot that starts wanting a slot eventually becomes that slot's holder, regardless of zone-lock contention or admin interference.

---- MODULE W4Od10m5p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Trains, NumBlocks, Controllers, QuorumSize

\* Quorum voting on each action: a train's move into the next block only
\* happens once enough controllers vote yes (or the admin overrides), and
\* each (train, block) clearance is recorded so it can never be granted twice.

Blocks == 1..NumBlocks

VARIABLES position, pendingMove, votes, clearanceCount

vars == <<position, pendingMove, votes, clearanceCount>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ position \in [Trains -> Blocks]
  /\ pendingMove \in [Trains -> 0..NumBlocks]
  /\ votes \in [Controllers -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ clearanceCount \in [Trains \X Blocks -> 0..2]

Init ==
  /\ position = [t \in Trains |-> 1]
  /\ pendingMove = [t \in Trains |-> 0]
  /\ votes = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]
  /\ clearanceCount = [t \in Trains, b \in Blocks |-> 0]

YesVotes == Cardinality({c \in Controllers : votes[c]})

\* Only one movement request is processed by the signalling office at a time.
RequestMove(t) ==
  /\ pendingMove[t] = 0
  /\ \A t2 \in Trains : pendingMove[t2] = 0
  /\ position[t] < NumBlocks
  /\ \A t2 \in Trains : position[t2] # position[t] + 1
  /\ pendingMove' = [pendingMove EXCEPT ![t] = position[t] + 1]
  /\ votes' = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<position, clearanceCount>>

CastVote(c) ==
  /\ \E t \in Trains : pendingMove[t] # 0
  /\ ~votes[c]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<position, pendingMove, clearanceCount>>

GrantClearance(t) ==
  /\ pendingMove[t] # 0
  /\ YesVotes >= QuorumSize
  /\ clearanceCount[t, pendingMove[t]] < 1
  /\ position' = [position EXCEPT ![t] = pendingMove[t]]
  /\ clearanceCount' = [clearanceCount EXCEPT ![t, pendingMove[t]] = @ + 1]
  /\ pendingMove' = [pendingMove EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
  /\ votes' = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]

\* Privileged admin override: force the pending movement through, bypassing
\* the vote count, but still subject to the same at-most-once bookkeeping.
AdminOverrideGrant(t) ==
  /\ pendingMove[t] # 0
  /\ clearanceCount[t, pendingMove[t]] < 1
  /\ position' = [position EXCEPT ![t] = pendingMove[t]]
  /\ clearanceCount' = [clearanceCount EXCEPT ![t, pendingMove[t]] = @ + 1]
  /\ pendingMove' = [pendingMove EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
  /\ votes' = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]

CancelRequest(t) ==
  /\ pendingMove[t] # 0
  /\ pendingMove' = [pendingMove EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
  /\ votes' = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<position, clearanceCount>>

\* Privileged admin override: always available, so a stuck vote can never
\* wedge the system even when no train has anything pending.
AdminAbortVotes ==
  /\ votes' = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<position, pendingMove, clearanceCount>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains : RequestMove(t)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : CastVote(c)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : GrantClearance(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : AdminOverrideGrant(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : CancelRequest(t)
  \/ AdminAbortVotes

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: a given train is granted clearance into a given block at most once.
AtMostOnceClearance == \A t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : clearanceCount[t, b] <= 1

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Trains = {t1, t2}
  NumBlocks = 4
  Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
  QuorumSize = 2

INVARIANT AtMostOnceClearance
nl:
This spec models a subway signalling block system for a short, one-way stretch of line
divided into numbered blocks. A train may move from the block it occupies into the next block
only after a quorum of signalling controllers votes to authorize that specific movement --
this is how the system prevents any single faulty controller from clearing a train into an
occupied or unsafe block on its own. Each movement request is voted on separately: a train
requests to move, controllers cast yes votes for that pending request, and once enough yes
votes have accumulated the movement is granted and the train physically advances into the new
block. Granting a movement into a given block for a given train is the irreversible act that
matters here: it may happen at most once per (train, block) pair, since the line is one-way
and a train is never expected to re-enter a block it has already been cleared into. A
privileged line controller (the admin) can bypass the quorum entirely in an emergency to force
a movement through immediately, and can also abort a stuck voting round at any time so the
system never wedges waiting for votes that will never arrive. The full action set is:
RequestMove (a train with no pending request asks to advance into the next block, provided
that block is not currently occupied by another train, and the vote tally for this new round
starts at zero), CastVote (any controller casts a yes vote for whichever movement is currently
pending), GrantClearance (once the yes votes for the pending movement reach the quorum size,
the train physically advances into the requested block and that block's clearance is recorded
as used), AdminOverrideGrant (the admin grants the pending movement immediately, bypassing the
vote count, subject to the same at-most-once clearance bookkeeping), CancelRequest (a train or
controller withdraws the current pending request without granting it), and AdminAbortVotes
(the admin clears every controller's yes vote for the current round, always available, so a
stalled vote can never permanently block the system).
SAFETY PROPERTY: for every train and every block, that train is granted clearance into that block at most once over the whole run.

---- MODULE W4Od9m4p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Feeders, MaxQueue

\* Bounded work queue with backpressure: `pending` may never grow past
\* MaxQueue. Shedding (or admin protection) is irreversible per feeder: once
\* retired into `shed` or `protected` a feeder never returns to `pending`.

VARIABLES pending, shed, protected, emergency

vars == <<pending, shed, protected, emergency>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ pending \subseteq Feeders
  /\ shed \subseteq Feeders
  /\ protected \subseteq Feeders
  /\ emergency \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ shed = {}
  /\ protected = {}
  /\ emergency = FALSE

AdmitFeeder(f) ==
  /\ f \notin pending
  /\ f \notin shed
  /\ f \notin protected
  /\ Cardinality(pending) < MaxQueue
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shed, protected, emergency>>

\* Shedding only ever happens while the grid emergency is in effect.
ShedFeeder(f) ==
  /\ emergency
  /\ f \in pending
  /\ pending' = pending \ {f}
  /\ shed' = shed \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<protected, emergency>>

\* Privileged admin override: protect a pending feeder from ever being shed,
\* whether or not an emergency is declared -- this is the backstop that keeps
\* every admitted feeder resolvable even if shedding never resumes.
AdminProtectFeeder(f) ==
  /\ f \in pending
  /\ pending' = pending \ {f}
  /\ protected' = protected \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shed, emergency>>

DeclareEmergency ==
  /\ ~emergency
  /\ emergency' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, shed, protected>>

EndEmergency ==
  /\ emergency
  /\ emergency' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, shed, protected>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : AdmitFeeder(f)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : ShedFeeder(f)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : AdminProtectFeeder(f)
  \/ DeclareEmergency
  \/ EndEmergency

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A f \in Feeders : WF_vars(AdminProtectFeeder(f))

\* SAFETY: each feeder is retired through exactly one irreversible path, and
\* a retired feeder never lingers in the pending queue.
ResolvedAtMostOnce ==
  \A f \in Feeders :
    /\ ~(f \in shed /\ f \in protected)
    /\ ((f \in shed \/ f \in protected) => f \notin pending)

\* LIVENESS: every admitted feeder is eventually retired one way or another,
\* even if the grid never declares another emergency (via admin protection).
EventualResolution == \A f \in Feeders : (f \in pending) ~> (f \in shed \/ f \in protected)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Feeders = {f1, f2, f3}
  MaxQueue = 2

INVARIANT ResolvedAtMostOnce
PROPERTY EventualResolution
nl:
This spec models a power-grid load shedder that manages a bounded work queue of feeder-shedding
requests during a period of high demand. When the grid is overloaded, feeders (individual
distribution circuits) are admitted into a pending queue of candidates for shedding, but that
queue has a fixed capacity: once it is full, no further feeder may be admitted until existing
requests are resolved (backpressure). While the grid controller has declared an emergency, the
shedder works through the pending queue, physically de-energizing (shedding) one feeder at a
time; shedding a feeder is the irreversible action for that feeder in this incident, and once a
feeder is shed it is retired from the process for good. A privileged grid admin can, at any
time, protect a pending feeder instead of letting it be shed -- for example because it feeds a
hospital -- which also permanently retires that feeder from the process without ever cutting
its power. The admin also controls whether the grid is formally in an emergency: shedding only
ever happens while the emergency is declared, but the admin's protection power works whether or
not an emergency is in effect, so a feeder can never be stuck forever with no way to be
resolved. The full action set is: AdmitFeeder (place a not-yet-seen feeder into the pending
queue, refused once the queue is at capacity), ShedFeeder (while an emergency is declared, take
one pending feeder and physically shed it, retiring it), AdminProtectFeeder (the admin removes
one pending feeder from the queue and marks it protected, retiring it without shedding it, in
or out of an emergency), DeclareEmergency (the admin formally declares the grid emergency, so
shedding may begin), and EndEmergency (the admin formally ends the emergency, so shedding
pauses).
SAFETY PROPERTY: no feeder is ever both shed and protected, and no feeder that has already been shed or protected is still sitting in the pending queue -- each feeder is retired through exactly one irreversible resolution.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every feeder admitted to the pending queue is eventually retired, either by being shed or by being protected by the admin, even if the grid never declares another emergency.

---- MODULE W4Od13m3p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Machines, MaxTerm, None

VARIABLES term, termLeader, localTerm, msgs, actsLog

vars == <<term, termLeader, localTerm, msgs, actsLog>>

Messages == [mtype: {"vote", "ann"}, mterm: 0..MaxTerm, mfrom: Machines]

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ termLeader \in [0..MaxTerm -> Machines \cup {None}]
  /\ localTerm \in [Machines -> 0..MaxTerm]
  /\ msgs \subseteq Messages
  /\ actsLog \subseteq (Machines \times (0..MaxTerm))

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ termLeader = [t \in 0..MaxTerm |-> None]
  /\ localTerm = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ msgs = {}
  /\ actsLog = {}

\* A caught-up machine bumps the term and broadcasts a vote message.
StartElection(m) ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ localTerm[m] = term
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ localTerm' = [localTerm EXCEPT ![m] = term + 1]
  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[mtype |-> "vote", mterm |-> term + 1, mfrom |-> m]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<termLeader, actsLog>>

\* Messages sit in an unordered set, so delivery may happen out of send order.
DeliverVote(n, msg) ==
  /\ msg \in msgs
  /\ msg.mtype = "vote"
  /\ msg.mterm > localTerm[n]
  /\ localTerm' = [localTerm EXCEPT ![n] = msg.mterm]
  /\ msgs' = msgs \ {msg}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, termLeader, actsLog>>

\* The candidate whose local view has caught up claims leadership permanently.
BecomeLeader(m) ==
  /\ localTerm[m] = term
  /\ term > 0
  /\ termLeader[term] = None
  /\ termLeader' = [termLeader EXCEPT ![term] = m]
  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[mtype |-> "ann", mterm |-> term, mfrom |-> m]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, localTerm, actsLog>>

DeliverAnnouncement(n, msg) ==
  /\ msg \in msgs
  /\ msg.mtype = "ann"
  /\ msg.mterm > localTerm[n]
  /\ localTerm' = [localTerm EXCEPT ![n] = msg.mterm]
  /\ msgs' = msgs \ {msg}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, termLeader, actsLog>>

\* Only a machine that is both caught up AND the recorded elected leader may act.
PerformAction(m) ==
  /\ localTerm[m] = term
  /\ termLeader[term] = m
  /\ actsLog' = actsLog \cup {<<m, term>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, termLeader, localTerm, msgs>>

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Machines : StartElection(m)
  \/ \E n \in Machines, msg \in msgs : DeliverVote(n, msg)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : BecomeLeader(m)
  \/ \E n \in Machines, msg \in msgs : DeliverAnnouncement(n, msg)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : PerformAction(m)

CONSTANTS
  Machines = {m1, m2, m3}
  MaxTerm = 2
  None = None

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoStaleAction
nl:
A network of vending machines shares a single restocking depot, and only one
machine at a time is allowed to draw from it, so the machines run a leader
election to decide who currently holds that privilege. Any machine can call a
StartElection when it believes the current term has stalled, which bumps the
network's term counter and broadcasts a vote message announcing the new term;
because the network can reorder messages in flight, these vote messages may
arrive at other machines in any order relative to when they were sent, not
necessarily the order they were broadcast. A machine that receives a vote
message for a term higher than its own local view runs DeliverVote and
adopts that newer term as its own. Once the machine that started an election
observes its own local term matches the network's current term, it may run
BecomeLeader, which permanently records it as the one true elected machine for
that term and broadcasts an announcement message. Other machines run
DeliverAnnouncement to adopt that term when they eventually receive the
(possibly delayed or reordered) announcement. Finally, a machine may run
PerformAction, physically dispensing from the shared depot, but only if its
own local term matches the network's current term and it is recorded as the
elected leader for that term -- this is what stops a machine that has fallen
behind (whose messages simply haven't caught up yet because of reordering) or
that was never elected from touching the shared depot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every dispense action ever performed was carried out by the machine that was truly and permanently recorded as the elected leader of the term during which the action happened, never by a stale or unelected machine.

CONSTANTS Workers, Jobs, MaxEpoch, None

VARIABLES shopLock, shopEpoch, workerEpoch, jobLock, printed

vars == <<shopLock, shopEpoch, workerEpoch, jobLock, printed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ shopLock \in Workers \cup {None}
  /\ shopEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ workerEpoch \in [Workers -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ jobLock \in [Jobs -> Workers \cup {None}]
  /\ printed \subseteq Jobs

Init ==
  /\ shopLock = None
  /\ shopEpoch = 0
  /\ workerEpoch = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
  /\ jobLock = [j \in Jobs |-> None]
  /\ printed = {}

\* Coarse lock: the whole spooler, taken only when free.
AcquireShopLock(w) ==
  /\ shopLock = None
  /\ shopLock' = w
  /\ workerEpoch' = [workerEpoch EXCEPT ![w] = shopEpoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shopEpoch, jobLock, printed>>

\* Fine lock: only the current coarse-lock holder, with matching epoch, may take it.
AcquireJobLock(w, j) ==
  /\ shopLock = w
  /\ workerEpoch[w] = shopEpoch
  /\ jobLock[j] = None
  /\ jobLock' = [jobLock EXCEPT ![j] = w]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shopLock, shopEpoch, workerEpoch, printed>>

PrintJob(w, j) ==
  /\ jobLock[j] = w
  /\ workerEpoch[w] = shopEpoch
  /\ printed' = printed \cup {j}
  /\ jobLock' = [jobLock EXCEPT ![j] = None]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shopLock, shopEpoch, workerEpoch>>

ReleaseShopLock(w) ==
  /\ shopLock = w
  /\ \A j \in Jobs : jobLock[j] # w
  /\ shopLock' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shopEpoch, workerEpoch, jobLock, printed>>

\* Privileged override: strip the coarse lock, free every job it held, bump the epoch.
AdminOverride ==
  /\ shopLock # None
  /\ shopEpoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ shopEpoch' = shopEpoch + 1
  /\ jobLock' = [j \in Jobs |-> IF jobLock[j] = shopLock THEN None ELSE jobLock[j]]
  /\ shopLock' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<workerEpoch, printed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E w \in Workers : AcquireShopLock(w)
  \/ \E w \in Workers, j \in Jobs : AcquireJobLock(w, j)
  \/ \E w \in Workers, j \in Jobs : PrintJob(w, j)
  \/ \E w \in Workers : ReleaseShopLock(w)
  \/ AdminOverride

Fairness == \A w \in Workers, j \in Jobs : WF_vars(PrintJob(w, j))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* No fine-locked job is ever held by a worker whose epoch has gone stale.
LockCoherence == \A j \in Jobs : jobLock[j] # None => workerEpoch[jobLock[j]] = shopEpoch

\* Every fine-locked job is eventually released, by printing or by override.
LivenessProperty == \A j \in Jobs : (jobLock[j] # None) ~> (jobLock[j] = None)

CONSTANTS
  Workers = {w1, w2}
  Jobs = {j1, j2, j3}
  MaxEpoch = 2
  None = None

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT LockCoherence
PROPERTY LivenessProperty
nl:
A print shop has one shared job spooler and a set of print-shop workers who
take turns operating it. Locking is hierarchical: a worker must first grab
the single coarse shop lock for the whole spooler before it may touch any
individual job, and only after holding the coarse lock may it grab a fine,
per-job lock on a specific print job. AcquireShopLock lets an idle worker
take the coarse lock when nobody else holds it. AcquireJobLock lets whichever
worker currently holds the coarse lock grab the fine lock on a specific job
that nobody else has locked. PrintJob lets the worker holding a job's fine
lock actually run the job to completion, which also releases that job's fine
lock. ReleaseShopLock lets a worker give up the coarse lock once it is not
holding any job's fine lock. Finally, AdminOverride is a privileged action a
shop supervisor can invoke at any time to forcibly strip the coarse lock away
from whoever currently holds it and free every job that worker had fine-
locked, bumping a shop-wide epoch counter so that the ousted worker's
credentials are immediately recognized as stale and cannot be used to touch
any job afterward, even if that worker's own view of the world hasn't caught
up yet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a print job is fine-locked, the worker holding that lock has credentials matching the shop's current epoch, so no stale or overridden worker's fine lock can linger after it has been stripped of authority.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every print job that becomes fine-locked is eventually released, either by being printed or by the supervisor's override reclaiming it.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Doctors, Patients, MaxRooms, Quorum, MaxOverrides

VARIABLES occupied, proposed, votes, overridesUsed

vars == <<occupied, proposed, votes, overridesUsed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ occupied \subseteq Patients
  /\ proposed \subseteq Patients
  /\ votes \in [Patients -> SUBSET Doctors]
  /\ occupied \cap proposed = {}
  /\ overridesUsed \in 0..MaxOverrides

Init ==
  /\ occupied = {}
  /\ proposed = {}
  /\ votes = [p \in Patients |-> {}]
  /\ overridesUsed = 0

\* Put a waiting patient up for a quorum vote.
Propose(p) ==
  /\ p \notin occupied
  /\ p \notin proposed
  /\ proposed' = proposed \cup {p}
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, overridesUsed>>

CastVote(d, p) ==
  /\ p \in proposed
  /\ d \notin votes[p]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = @ \cup {d}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, proposed, overridesUsed>>

\* Quorum reached AND a room is free: move the patient in.
Admit(p) ==
  /\ p \in proposed
  /\ Cardinality(votes[p]) >= Quorum
  /\ Cardinality(occupied) < MaxRooms
  /\ occupied' = occupied \cup {p}
  /\ proposed' = proposed \ {p}
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED overridesUsed

\* Always available: no ballot required, keeps the schedule from wedging.
Discharge(p) ==
  /\ p \in occupied
  /\ occupied' = occupied \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, votes, overridesUsed>>

\* Privileged bypass, still bounded by the same room capacity and a finite override budget.
AdminOverride(p) ==
  /\ p \notin occupied
  /\ Cardinality(occupied) < MaxRooms
  /\ overridesUsed < MaxOverrides
  /\ occupied' = occupied \cup {p}
  /\ proposed' = proposed \ {p}
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
  /\ overridesUsed' = overridesUsed + 1

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Patients : Propose(p)
  \/ \E d \in Doctors, p \in Patients : CastVote(d, p)
  \/ \E p \in Patients : Admit(p)
  \/ \E p \in Patients : Discharge(p)
  \/ \E p \in Patients : AdminOverride(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The assigned property itself: occupied operating rooms never exceed capacity.
CapacityInvariant == Cardinality(occupied) <= MaxRooms

CONSTANTS
  Doctors = {d1, d2}
  Patients = {p1, p2, p3}
  MaxRooms = 2
  Quorum = 2
  MaxOverrides = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CapacityInvariant
nl:
A hospital has a fixed, small number of operating rooms shared among several
surgeons who together form the scheduling committee, and admitting a patient
into surgery normally requires a quorum of the committee to sign off first.
Propose lets any committee member put a waiting patient forward as a
candidate for the next open operating room, starting an empty ballot for that
patient. CastVote lets a committee member who has not already voted for a
proposed patient add their vote to that patient's ballot. Admit moves a
proposed patient into an operating room, but only once that patient's ballot
has reached quorum and there is a free operating room to put them in; admitting
clears the patient's ballot. Discharge frees up an operating room by moving a
patient who has finished surgery back out, and is always available so the
schedule can never wedge with every room full and nobody leaving. Finally,
AdminOverride is a privileged action the chief of surgery can invoke to rush a
patient straight into an open operating room in an emergency, completely
skipping the quorum ballot -- but even the chief of surgery cannot invoke it
when every operating room is already full, and the hospital only authorizes
the chief a limited number of such emergency overrides in total.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of patients simultaneously occupying operating rooms never exceeds the fixed number of operating rooms the hospital actually has, whether patients arrived through quorum vote or the chief's emergency override.

---- MODULE W4Od12m7p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Hospitals, TotalUnits, MaxReq

VARIABLES shelf, reserved, snapshot, used

vars == <<shelf, reserved, snapshot, used>>

\* Sum of a bounded function's range over a finite set of hospitals.
RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET h == CHOOSE h \in S : TRUE
       IN f[h] + SumOver(f, S \ {h})

TypeOK ==
  /\ shelf \in 0..TotalUnits
  /\ reserved \in [Hospitals -> 0..TotalUnits]
  /\ snapshot \in [Hospitals -> 0..TotalUnits]
  /\ used \in 0..TotalUnits

Init ==
  /\ shelf = TotalUnits
  /\ reserved = [h \in Hospitals |-> 0]
  /\ snapshot = [h \in Hospitals |-> TotalUnits]
  /\ used = 0

\* Catch-up: always lets a hospital refresh its view to the live shelf count.
Resync(h) ==
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![h] = shelf]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, reserved, used>>

\* The compare-and-swap: only fires if the remembered snapshot is still current.
CasReserve(h, amt) ==
  /\ amt \in 1..MaxReq
  /\ snapshot[h] = shelf
  /\ shelf >= amt
  /\ shelf' = shelf - amt
  /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![h] = @ + amt]
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![h] = shelf - amt]
  /\ UNCHANGED used

Issue(h, amt) ==
  /\ amt \in 1..MaxReq
  /\ reserved[h] >= amt
  /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![h] = @ - amt]
  /\ used' = used + amt
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, snapshot>>

\* Privileged bypass: moves units without touching or checking any snapshot,
\* which is exactly what can strand other hospitals' snapshots as stale.
AdminOverride(h, amt) ==
  /\ amt \in 1..MaxReq
  /\ shelf >= amt
  /\ shelf' = shelf - amt
  /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![h] = @ + amt]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snapshot, used>>

Next ==
  \/ \E h \in Hospitals : Resync(h)
  \/ \E h \in Hospitals, amt \in 1..MaxReq : CasReserve(h, amt)
  \/ \E h \in Hospitals, amt \in 1..MaxReq : Issue(h, amt)
  \/ \E h \in Hospitals, amt \in 1..MaxReq : AdminOverride(h, amt)

Fairness == \A h \in Hospitals : WF_vars(Resync(h))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* Nothing is ever created or destroyed, only moved between the three bins.
Conservation == shelf + used + SumOver(reserved, Hospitals) = TotalUnits

\* A hospital that falls out of sync with the shelf always eventually catches up.
LivenessProperty == \A h \in Hospitals : (snapshot[h] # shelf) ~> (snapshot[h] = shelf)

CONSTANTS
  Hospitals = {h1, h2}
  TotalUnits = 3
  MaxReq = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT Conservation
PROPERTY LivenessProperty
nl:
A blood bank keeps a single shared shelf count of blood units, and each
partner hospital keeps its own locally reserved stock plus a remembered
snapshot of what it last saw on the shelf. Reservations are done through a
compare-and-swap register: a hospital may only pull units off the shelf
through CasReserve, and that action only goes through if the hospital's
remembered snapshot still equals the shelf's actual current count -- if some
other hospital (or the director) has changed the shelf in the meantime, the
attempt is out of date and does nothing until the hospital catches up. Resync
lets a hospital refresh its remembered snapshot to match whatever the shelf
currently holds, which is how a hospital that has fallen behind catches back
up so its next compare-and-swap attempt can go through. Issue lets a hospital
consume some of its own already-reserved units for a transfusion, moving them
out of the reserved pool into permanently-used units, never destroying them
from the tracker's books. Finally, AdminOverride is a privileged action the
bank director can invoke to move units directly from the shelf into a
hospital's reserved stock without going through the compare-and-swap check at
all, which is exactly what can leave other hospitals' remembered snapshots
out of date.

SAFETY PROPERTY: at every moment, the shelf count plus every hospital's reserved units plus all units already used together equal the blood bank's fixed total supply, so no unit is ever created or destroyed, only moved.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: whenever a hospital's remembered snapshot falls out of date with the shelf's actual count, that hospital eventually resyncs and catches back up to the current shelf count.

---- MODULE W4Od16m8p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Pharmacists, Prescriptions, None

VARIABLES cabinetHolder, pending, rxLock, dispenseCount

vars == <<cabinetHolder, pending, rxLock, dispenseCount>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ cabinetHolder \in Pharmacists \cup {None}
  /\ pending \subseteq Pharmacists
  /\ rxLock \in [Prescriptions -> Pharmacists \cup {None}]
  /\ dispenseCount \in [Prescriptions -> 0..1]

Init ==
  /\ cabinetHolder = None
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ rxLock = [rx \in Prescriptions |-> None]
  /\ dispenseCount = [rx \in Prescriptions |-> 0]

\* Requests just join an unordered pool -- there is no send order to respect.
RequestCabinet(p) ==
  /\ p \notin pending
  /\ cabinetHolder # p
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinetHolder, rxLock, dispenseCount>>

\* Any pending request may be serviced next, so grants can happen out of order.
GrantCabinet(p) ==
  /\ p \in pending
  /\ cabinetHolder = None
  /\ cabinetHolder' = p
  /\ pending' = pending \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rxLock, dispenseCount>>

\* Fine lock beneath the coarse one: only the coarse holder may take it.
LockPrescription(p, rx) ==
  /\ cabinetHolder = p
  /\ rxLock[rx] = None
  /\ rxLock' = [rxLock EXCEPT ![rx] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinetHolder, pending, dispenseCount>>

\* The irreversible step, guarded so it can only ever fire once per prescription.
Dispense(p, rx) ==
  /\ rxLock[rx] = p
  /\ dispenseCount[rx] = 0
  /\ dispenseCount' = [dispenseCount EXCEPT ![rx] = @ + 1]
  /\ rxLock' = [rxLock EXCEPT ![rx] = None]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinetHolder, pending>>

\* Lets a pharmacist give up a fine lock it no longer needs (e.g. already
\* dispensed, or it changed its mind) without touching the coarse lock.
UnlockPrescription(p, rx) ==
  /\ rxLock[rx] = p
  /\ rxLock' = [rxLock EXCEPT ![rx] = None]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinetHolder, pending, dispenseCount>>

ReleaseCabinet(p) ==
  /\ cabinetHolder = p
  /\ \A rx \in Prescriptions : rxLock[rx] # p
  /\ cabinetHolder' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, rxLock, dispenseCount>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Pharmacists : RequestCabinet(p)
  \/ \E p \in Pharmacists : GrantCabinet(p)
  \/ \E p \in Pharmacists, rx \in Prescriptions : LockPrescription(p, rx)
  \/ \E p \in Pharmacists, rx \in Prescriptions : Dispense(p, rx)
  \/ \E p \in Pharmacists, rx \in Prescriptions : UnlockPrescription(p, rx)
  \/ \E p \in Pharmacists : ReleaseCabinet(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The assigned property itself: each prescription is dispensed at most once.
AtMostOnce == \A rx \in Prescriptions : dispenseCount[rx] <= 1

====
nl:
A pharmacy has a single shared dispensing cabinet and a set of pharmacists who
must take turns using it, with locking done in two tiers: a coarse lock on the
whole cabinet, and beneath that, a fine lock on each individual prescription.
RequestCabinet lets a pharmacist put in a request to use the cabinet, and
because pharmacist requests just sit together in an unordered pool waiting to
be handled, GrantCabinet can service any pending request out of turn -- a
request filed later can be granted before one filed earlier, exactly as if the
requests were messages that got reordered in transit. Once a pharmacist holds
the coarse cabinet lock, LockPrescription lets it take the fine lock on one
specific prescription that nobody else currently has locked. Dispense is the
irreversible step: the pharmacist holding a prescription's fine lock actually
counts out and hands over that medication, and it releases the fine lock when
done. UnlockPrescription lets a pharmacist give up a prescription's fine lock
without dispensing anything, whether because it already dispensed it earlier
or simply changed its mind about which prescription to handle next.
ReleaseCabinet lets a pharmacist give up the coarse cabinet lock once it is
not holding any prescription's fine lock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no prescription is ever dispensed more than once, no matter how out of order the cabinet requests that led up to it were granted.

---- MODULE W4Od18m2p3t1 ----
\* Smart-home door lock network: a coordinator runs two-phase commit to allocate
\* a time slot to one lock at a time. Votes are collected via an unordered
\* message set, so the network may deliver them in any order (reordering twist).
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Locks, Slots

VARIABLES phase, propOwner, votes, msgs, allocLog

vars == <<phase, propOwner, votes, msgs, allocLog>>

NoneLock == "none"

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in [Slots -> {"idle", "proposing"}]
  /\ propOwner \in [Slots -> Locks \cup {NoneLock}]
  /\ votes \in [Slots -> [Locks -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]]
  /\ msgs \subseteq (Slots \X Locks \X {"yes", "no"})
  /\ allocLog \subseteq (Slots \X Locks)

Init ==
  /\ phase = [s \in Slots |-> "idle"]
  /\ propOwner = [s \in Slots |-> NoneLock]
  /\ votes = [s \in Slots |-> [l \in Locks |-> "none"]]
  /\ msgs = {}
  /\ allocLog = {}

IsAllocated(s) == \E l \in Locks : <<s, l>> \in allocLog

\* Coordinator begins a 2PC round to allocate a currently-free slot to lock l.
Propose(s, l) ==
  /\ phase[s] = "idle"
  /\ ~IsAllocated(s)
  /\ propOwner' = [propOwner EXCEPT ![s] = l]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![s] = "proposing"]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = [k \in Locks |-> "none"]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<msgs, allocLog>>

\* Lock l casts its vote for the round; the vote enters the network as a
\* message and is not applied until delivered, so it can be reordered.
SendVote(s, l) ==
  /\ phase[s] = "proposing"
  /\ votes[s][l] = "none"
  /\ ~(\E m \in msgs : m[1] = s /\ m[2] = l)
  /\ \E choice \in {"yes", "no"} : msgs' = msgs \cup {<<s, l, choice>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, propOwner, votes, allocLog>>

\* Network delivers the pending vote message for (s,l), if any -- delivery of
\* distinct messages is independent, so messages may be applied out of order.
DeliverVote(s, l) ==
  /\ votes[s][l] = "none"
  /\ \E m \in msgs :
       /\ m[1] = s /\ m[2] = l
       /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s][l] = m[3]]
       /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, propOwner, allocLog>>

\* All locks agreed: commit the allocation permanently into the log.
Commit(s) ==
  /\ phase[s] = "proposing"
  /\ \A l \in Locks : votes[s][l] = "yes"
  /\ allocLog' = allocLog \cup {<<s, propOwner[s]>>}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]
  /\ msgs' = {m \in msgs : m[1] # s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<propOwner, votes>>

\* Some lock refused: abort the round, clearing any stale in-flight votes.
Abort(s) ==
  /\ phase[s] = "proposing"
  /\ \E l \in Locks : votes[s][l] = "no"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]
  /\ propOwner' = [propOwner EXCEPT ![s] = NoneLock]
  /\ msgs' = {m \in msgs : m[1] # s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, allocLog>>

\* An allocated slot's tenancy ends, freeing it for a future round (keeps
\* the system live instead of freezing once every slot is allocated).
Free(s) ==
  /\ IsAllocated(s)
  /\ allocLog' = {p \in allocLog : p[1] # s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, propOwner, votes, msgs>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Slots, l \in Locks : Propose(s, l)
  \/ \E s \in Slots, l \in Locks : SendVote(s, l)
  \/ \E s \in Slots, l \in Locks : DeliverVote(s, l)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Commit(s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Abort(s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Free(s)

Fairness ==
  /\ \A s \in Slots, l \in Locks : WF_vars(SendVote(s, l))
  /\ \A s \in Slots, l \in Locks : WF_vars(DeliverVote(s, l))
  /\ \A s \in Slots : WF_vars(Commit(s))
  /\ \A s \in Slots : WF_vars(Abort(s))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: the allocation log never records two different locks owning the same slot.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A s \in Slots : \A l1, l2 \in Locks :
     (<<s, l1>> \in allocLog /\ <<s, l2>> \in allocLog) => l1 = l2

\* LIVENESS: every round that enters "proposing" for a slot eventually leaves it.
EventuallyResolved == \A s \in Slots : (phase[s] = "proposing") ~> (phase[s] # "proposing")
====
nl:
This models a smart-home door lock network that allocates shared access time
slots to individual locks using a two-phase commit protocol. A coordinator
begins a round by proposing that one lock take over a currently free slot
(Propose). Each lock in the network then casts its vote on whether the
proposal is acceptable, but the vote is only placed on the network as a
message rather than applied immediately (SendVote); because the network can
reorder messages, a delivery action (DeliverVote) may apply any lock's
pending vote for a given slot whenever it happens to arrive, independent of
the order in which votes were sent. Once every lock in the network has voted
"yes" for a round, the coordinator commits the allocation, permanently
recording which lock now owns that slot (Commit). If any lock voted "no",
the round is aborted and any stale in-flight vote messages for that slot are
discarded so a fresh round can start cleanly (Abort). Finally, an allocated
slot's tenancy can end, freeing it up again for a future allocation round
(Free), which is what keeps the network able to keep running rounds instead
of freezing once every slot has been claimed once.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At any point in time, the allocation log never records two
different locks as the current owner of the same slot.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every round that begins proposing an allocation for a
slot eventually leaves the proposing state, being either committed or
aborted, no matter how the network reorders the vote messages.

---- MODULE W4Od5m3p4t2 ----
\* Two independent matchmaker instances share a single lobby pool. Each
\* instance can win a failover election over a shared epoch register; only an
\* instance whose remembered epoch matches the current register may admit
\* players, which is what prevents a stale (post-crash) leader from
\* over-filling the shared pool.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, MaxCapacity, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, instanceEpoch, crashed, poolCount

vars == <<epoch, instanceEpoch, crashed, poolCount>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ instanceEpoch \in [Instances -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ crashed \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ poolCount \in 0..MaxCapacity

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ instanceEpoch = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
  /\ crashed = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
  /\ poolCount = 0

\* A live instance wins a failover election, bumping the one shared epoch
\* register it must later present a matching belief for in order to admit.
Elect(i) ==
  /\ ~crashed[i]
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ instanceEpoch' = [instanceEpoch EXCEPT ![i] = epoch + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, poolCount>>

Crash(i) ==
  /\ ~crashed[i]
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, instanceEpoch, poolCount>>

\* A crashed instance rejoins the network but keeps its stale pre-crash epoch
\* belief (no automatic resync) -- this is the source of split-brain risk.
Recover(i) ==
  /\ crashed[i]
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, instanceEpoch, poolCount>>

\* Instance i admits a player into the shared pool -- only valid while its
\* remembered epoch still matches the current shared register.
Admit(i) ==
  /\ ~crashed[i]
  /\ epoch > 0
  /\ instanceEpoch[i] = epoch
  /\ poolCount < MaxCapacity
  /\ poolCount' = poolCount + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, instanceEpoch, crashed>>

Leave ==
  /\ poolCount > 0
  /\ poolCount' = poolCount - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, instanceEpoch, crashed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Instances : Elect(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : Crash(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : Recover(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : Admit(i)
  \/ Leave

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: the shared lobby pool never holds more players than its declared capacity.
BoundedCapacity == poolCount <= MaxCapacity
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Instances = {i1, i2}
  MaxCapacity = 3
  MaxEpoch = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
nl:
This models a multiplayer game lobby matchmaker made of two independent
matchmaker instances that share a single lobby pool with a fixed capacity.
Leadership over the shared pool is decided by failover elections against one
shared epoch register: any instance that is currently up can win an election
(Elect), which bumps the shared epoch and records that instance's own belief
that it is now the current leader at that new epoch number. An instance can
crash at any time (Crash), simulating an outage, and a crashed instance can
later rejoin the network (Recover) -- but recovering does not automatically
refresh its memory of the epoch, so a recovered instance may still believe it
is leader at an old, now-superseded epoch. Whichever instance is up and whose
remembered epoch still matches the current shared epoch register is allowed
to admit a new player into the shared lobby pool (Admit); an instance whose
memory has fallen behind (because someone else won a later election while it
was down) is blocked from admitting until it wins its own new election.
Players can also leave the shared pool at any time (Leave), freeing up room.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared lobby pool never holds more players than its
declared capacity, even though two independent matchmaker instances are both
able to attempt admissions against it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m0p6t5 ----
\* Subway signalling blocks are claimed with optimistic locking: a train reads
\* a block's version stamp, and may only claim/act on the block if its cached
\* copy still matches. A privileged admin can force-lock (and later clear) a
\* block, bypassing the normal optimistic check entirely.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks, MaxVersion

VARIABLES version, owner, cached, overrideActive

vars == <<version, owner, cached, overrideActive>>

NoneTrain == "none"

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in [Blocks -> 0..MaxVersion]
  /\ owner \in [Blocks -> Trains \cup {NoneTrain}]
  /\ cached \in [Trains -> [Blocks -> 0..MaxVersion]]
  /\ overrideActive \in [Blocks -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ version = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
  /\ owner = [b \in Blocks |-> NoneTrain]
  /\ cached = [t \in Trains |-> [b \in Blocks |-> 0]]
  /\ overrideActive = [b \in Blocks |-> FALSE]

\* Train t re-reads block b's version stamp, the retry step of optimistic locking.
ReadBlock(t, b) ==
  /\ cached[t][b] # version[b]
  /\ cached' = [cached EXCEPT ![t][b] = version[b]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner, overrideActive>>

\* Train t claims free block b -- only succeeds while its cached version is
\* still current (the optimistic-lock check) and no admin lockout is active.
ClaimBlock(t, b) ==
  /\ ~overrideActive[b]
  /\ owner[b] = NoneTrain
  /\ cached[t][b] = version[b]
  /\ version[b] < MaxVersion
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = t]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = version[b] + 1]
  /\ cached' = [cached EXCEPT ![t][b] = version[b] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED overrideActive

ReleaseBlock(t, b) ==
  /\ owner[b] = t
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = NoneTrain]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, cached, overrideActive>>

\* Admin forcibly locks out block b, clearing any current occupant regardless
\* of that train's optimistic-lock state -- the privileged bypass.
AdminOverride(b) ==
  /\ ~overrideActive[b]
  /\ overrideActive' = [overrideActive EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = NoneTrain]
  /\ version' = IF version[b] < MaxVersion
                 THEN [version EXCEPT ![b] = version[b] + 1]
                 ELSE version
  /\ UNCHANGED cached

AdminClear(b) ==
  /\ overrideActive[b]
  /\ overrideActive' = [overrideActive EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, version, cached>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : ReadBlock(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : ClaimBlock(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : ReleaseBlock(t, b)
  \/ \E b \in Blocks : AdminOverride(b)
  \/ \E b \in Blocks : AdminClear(b)

Fairness == \A t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : WF_vars(ReadBlock(t, b))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: whichever train currently owns a block, its cached version always
\* matches that block's real version -- a stale participant can never hold it.
NoStaleOwnership ==
  \A b \in Blocks : \A t \in Trains : owner[b] = t => cached[t][b] = version[b]

\* LIVENESS: a train whose cached copy of a block has gone stale eventually
\* catches up to the block's current version.
TrainsCatchUp ==
  \A t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : (cached[t][b] # version[b]) ~> (cached[t][b] = version[b])
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Trains = {t1, t2}
  Blocks = {b1, b2}
  MaxVersion = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoStaleOwnership

PROPERTY TrainsCatchUp
nl:
This models a subway signalling block system where each track block is
guarded by optimistic locking instead of a traditional exclusive lock. Every
block carries a version stamp. A train can re-read a block's current version
stamp into its own cache at any time (ReadBlock), which is exactly the retry
step of optimistic locking after a failed attempt. A train may claim a free
block (ClaimBlock) only if its cached version still matches the block's real
current version and no admin lockout is in effect; a successful claim bumps
the block's version, which makes every other train's cached copy of that
block stale until they re-read it. A train that currently owns a block can
release it (ReleaseBlock). Separately, a signalling-room admin holds a
privileged override: the admin can force a lockout on any block at any time
(AdminOverride), immediately evicting whichever train currently occupies it
regardless of that train's optimistic-lock state, and later lift the lockout
(AdminClear) to let normal optimistic claiming resume.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whichever train currently owns a block, that train's cached
version of the block always matches the block's real current version, so no
unauthorized or stale train can ever be the recorded occupant of a block.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: A train whose cached copy of a block has fallen behind
the block's real version always eventually catches up and re-reads the
current version.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m1p0t5 ----
\* A network of vending machines arranged in a fixed ring passes a single
\* token around to decide who may use the shared cash/restock mechanism. A
\* privileged admin can also seize exclusive access directly, bypassing the
\* ring order entirely, but must still respect mutual exclusion.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS N

Machines == 1..N
succ(m) == IF m = N THEN 1 ELSE m + 1
Admin == 0

VARIABLES tokenHolder, holders, adminLock, requesting

vars == <<tokenHolder, holders, adminLock, requesting>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ tokenHolder \in Machines
  /\ holders \subseteq (Machines \cup {Admin})
  /\ adminLock \in BOOLEAN
  /\ requesting \in [Machines -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ tokenHolder = 1
  /\ holders = {}
  /\ adminLock = FALSE
  /\ requesting = [m \in Machines |-> FALSE]

\* Machine m signals it wants to use the shared resource.
Request(m) ==
  /\ ~requesting[m]
  /\ requesting' = [requesting EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, holders, adminLock>>

\* Only the current token holder, with a pending request and no admin lock
\* in effect, may enter and actually use the shared resource.
Enter(m) ==
  /\ tokenHolder = m
  /\ requesting[m]
  /\ ~adminLock
  /\ holders = {}
  /\ holders' = holders \cup {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, adminLock, requesting>>

Exit(m) ==
  /\ m \in holders
  /\ holders' = holders \ {m}
  /\ requesting' = [requesting EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, adminLock>>

\* The token moves on around the fixed ring once nobody is using the resource.
PassToken ==
  /\ holders = {}
  /\ ~adminLock
  /\ tokenHolder' = succ(tokenHolder)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, adminLock, requesting>>

\* Admin seizes exclusive access directly, bypassing the ring's token order.
AdminSeize ==
  /\ holders = {}
  /\ ~adminLock
  /\ adminLock' = TRUE
  /\ holders' = holders \cup {Admin}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, requesting>>

AdminRelease ==
  /\ adminLock
  /\ adminLock' = FALSE
  /\ holders' = holders \ {Admin}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, requesting>>

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Request(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Enter(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Exit(m)
  \/ PassToken
  \/ AdminSeize
  \/ AdminRelease

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: at most one participant -- a machine or the admin -- ever holds
\* the shared resource at the same time.
MutualExclusion == Cardinality(holders) <= 1
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  N = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
This models a network of vending machines arranged in a fixed ring that
share one physical cash and restock mechanism. Exactly one token circulates
around the ring, and only whoever currently holds the token may use the
shared mechanism. A machine first signals that it wants to use the mechanism
(Request). Whichever machine currently holds the token, has an outstanding
request, and finds no admin lockout in effect may then actually enter and
use the shared mechanism (Enter); when it is done it steps back out (Exit).
When nobody is using the mechanism and no admin lockout is in effect, the
token moves on to the next machine in the ring (PassToken). Separately, a
network administrator holds a privileged override: whenever nobody is
currently using the mechanism, the admin can seize it directly (AdminSeize),
bypassing the ring's token order entirely and blocking ordinary machines
from entering until the admin is done, and later give it back (AdminRelease)
so ordinary ring operation resumes.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one participant -- an ordinary machine or the
admin -- ever holds and uses the shared mechanism at the same time, even
though the admin can seize it outside the normal token order.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m8p2t4 ----
\* A university registration system uses hierarchical locking: a student must
\* first hold the coarse registry-wide lock, then the fine per-course lock,
\* before a seat can be granted or denied. Course capacity can also be
\* changed at runtime by the registrar, so the conserved quantity is the
\* relationship between seats used and the currently declared capacity.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, Courses, MaxCap

NoneStudent == "none"

VARIABLES registryLock, courseLock, enrolledBy, capacity

vars == <<registryLock, courseLock, enrolledBy, capacity>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ registryLock \in Students \cup {NoneStudent}
  /\ courseLock \in [Courses -> Students \cup {NoneStudent}]
  /\ enrolledBy \in [Courses -> SUBSET Students]
  /\ capacity \in [Courses -> 0..MaxCap]

Init ==
  /\ registryLock = NoneStudent
  /\ courseLock = [c \in Courses |-> NoneStudent]
  /\ enrolledBy = [c \in Courses |-> {}]
  /\ capacity = [c \in Courses |-> MaxCap]

\* A student begins a registration attempt by taking the coarse, registry-wide lock.
AcquireCoarse(s) ==
  /\ registryLock = NoneStudent
  /\ registryLock' = s
  /\ UNCHANGED <<courseLock, enrolledBy, capacity>>

\* While holding the coarse lock, the student takes the fine lock on one
\* specific course section (and only one at a time).
AcquireFine(s, c) ==
  /\ registryLock = s
  /\ courseLock[c] = NoneStudent
  /\ ~(\E c2 \in Courses : courseLock[c2] = s)
  /\ courseLock' = [courseLock EXCEPT ![c] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<registryLock, enrolledBy, capacity>>

\* Holding both locks, the student is enrolled if there is room, or is turned
\* away if the course is full; either way both locks are then released.
EnrollOrReject(s, c) ==
  /\ registryLock = s
  /\ courseLock[c] = s
  /\ enrolledBy' = [enrolledBy EXCEPT ![c] =
                      IF s \in @ THEN @
                      ELSE IF Cardinality(@) < capacity[c] THEN @ \cup {s} ELSE @]
  /\ courseLock' = [courseLock EXCEPT ![c] = NoneStudent]
  /\ registryLock' = NoneStudent
  /\ UNCHANGED capacity

\* A student can drop an enrolled course at any time, freeing the seat.
Drop(s, c) ==
  /\ s \in enrolledBy[c]
  /\ enrolledBy' = [enrolledBy EXCEPT ![c] = @ \ {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<registryLock, courseLock, capacity>>

\* The registrar can grow a section's capacity at runtime.
IncreaseCapacity(c) ==
  /\ capacity[c] < MaxCap
  /\ capacity' = [capacity EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<registryLock, courseLock, enrolledBy>>

\* The registrar can shrink a section's capacity, but never below how many
\* students are already enrolled in it.
DecreaseCapacity(c) ==
  /\ capacity[c] > Cardinality(enrolledBy[c])
  /\ capacity' = [capacity EXCEPT ![c] = @ - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<registryLock, courseLock, enrolledBy>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Students : AcquireCoarse(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students, c \in Courses : AcquireFine(s, c)
  \/ \E s \in Students, c \in Courses : EnrollOrReject(s, c)
  \/ \E s \in Students, c \in Courses : Drop(s, c)
  \/ \E c \in Courses : IncreaseCapacity(c)
  \/ \E c \in Courses : DecreaseCapacity(c)

Fairness ==
  /\ \A s \in Students, c \in Courses : WF_vars(AcquireFine(s, c))
  /\ \A s \in Students, c \in Courses : WF_vars(EnrollOrReject(s, c))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: no course section is ever holding more enrolled students than its
\* currently declared capacity, even as that capacity changes at runtime.
SeatConservation == \A c \in Courses : Cardinality(enrolledBy[c]) <= capacity[c]

\* LIVENESS: a student who begins a registration attempt (holding the coarse
\* lock) always eventually finishes that attempt and releases it.
AttemptsResolve == \A s \in Students : (registryLock = s) ~> (registryLock # s)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Students = {s1, s2}
  Courses = {c1, c2}
  MaxCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SeatConservation

PROPERTY AttemptsResolve
nl:
This models a university course-registration system that uses hierarchical
locking: a coarse, registry-wide lock must be acquired before a fine,
per-course lock, before any seat decision is made. A student begins a
registration attempt by taking the single coarse registry lock, which only
one student can hold at a time (AcquireCoarse). While holding it, the
student takes the fine lock on one specific course section, and can only
hold one course's fine lock at a time (AcquireFine). Once both locks are
held, the attempt is resolved: the student is enrolled if the section still
has room, or turned away if it is full, and either way both locks are
immediately released so the next student's attempt can proceed
(EnrollOrReject). A student can drop a course they are already enrolled in
at any time, freeing the seat back up (Drop). Independently of the locking
protocol, the registrar can change a course section's capacity at runtime:
growing it (IncreaseCapacity) whenever there is still room to grow, or
shrinking it (DecreaseCapacity) but never below however many students are
currently enrolled in that section.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No course section's enrolled-student count ever exceeds its
currently declared capacity, even as the registrar changes that capacity
while students are registering.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every student who begins a registration attempt by taking
the coarse registry lock always eventually finishes that attempt, going
through the fine lock and a seat decision, and releases the locks.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m1p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* Two independent baggage-routing rings (Ring A, Ring B) each grant exclusive
\* "gate" access to their conveyor via a circulating token, and both rings
\* draw bags from and return bags to one shared holding pool. Advancing a
\* token never moves a bag; only the station holding the token may inject or
\* eject a bag between its ring and the shared pool.

CONSTANTS NA, NB, Total

VARIABLES pool, tokA, tokB, loadA, loadB

vars == <<pool, tokA, tokB, loadA, loadB>>

TypeOK == /\ pool \in 0..Total
          /\ loadA \in 0..Total
          /\ loadB \in 0..Total
          /\ tokA \in 1..NA
          /\ tokB \in 1..NB

Init == /\ pool = Total
        /\ tokA = 1
        /\ tokB = 1
        /\ loadA = 0
        /\ loadB = 0

AdvanceTokenA == /\ tokA' = (tokA % NA) + 1
                 /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, tokB, loadA, loadB>>

AdvanceTokenB == /\ tokB' = (tokB % NB) + 1
                 /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, tokA, loadA, loadB>>

\* Only the gate station (position 1) of a ring may exchange a bag with the pool.
InjectA == /\ tokA = 1
           /\ pool > 0
           /\ pool' = pool - 1
           /\ loadA' = loadA + 1
           /\ UNCHANGED <<tokA, tokB, loadB>>

EjectA == /\ tokA = 1
          /\ loadA > 0
          /\ loadA' = loadA - 1
          /\ pool' = pool + 1
          /\ UNCHANGED <<tokA, tokB, loadB>>

InjectB == /\ tokB = 1
           /\ pool > 0
           /\ pool' = pool - 1
           /\ loadB' = loadB + 1
           /\ UNCHANGED <<tokA, tokB, loadA>>

EjectB == /\ tokB = 1
          /\ loadB > 0
          /\ loadB' = loadB - 1
          /\ pool' = pool + 1
          /\ UNCHANGED <<tokA, tokB, loadA>>

Next == AdvanceTokenA \/ AdvanceTokenB \/ InjectA \/ EjectA \/ InjectB \/ EjectB

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Nothing is ever created or destroyed: pool + Ring A load + Ring B load is fixed.
Conservation == pool + loadA + loadB = Total

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NA = 3
    NB = 3
    Total = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
This spec models an airport baggage router built from two independent token-ring conveyor loops, Ring A and Ring B, that both draw bags from and return bags to one shared holding pool. Each ring is a cycle of conveyor stations; a single access token circulates around each ring's stations in a fixed rotation, and only the station currently holding the token - the ring's gate station - may exchange a bag with the shared pool. The action set is: AdvanceTokenA and AdvanceTokenB advance each ring's token to the next station in its own rotation, granting exclusive gate access to whichever station takes over; InjectA and InjectB, enabled only when Ring A's (resp. Ring B's) token sits at the gate station and the shared pool holds at least one bag, move one bag out of the shared pool onto that ring's conveyor; EjectA and EjectB, enabled only when the token sits at the gate and that ring is currently carrying at least one bag, move one bag off the ring's conveyor back into the shared pool. Because the two rings never inject or eject more than one bag at a time and always exchange with the same shared pool, the total number of bags anywhere in the system - on Ring A, on Ring B, or sitting in the shared pool - never changes.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of bags in the shared pool plus the number of bags on Ring A's conveyor plus the number of bags on Ring B's conveyor always equals the fixed total number of bags in the system (nothing is created or destroyed by either ring).

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m5p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Two independent runway-closure decisions (A and B) each require a quorum
\* vote from one shared pool of duty controllers. A controller's attention is
\* a shared resource: once they vote for one runway they cannot also vote for
\* the other. Committing a closure is irreversible and may fire at most once
\* per runway, exactly when its quorum has actually been reached.

CONSTANTS Controllers, Quorum
ASSUME Quorum \in Nat

VARIABLES votesA, votesB, closedA, closedB

vars == <<votesA, votesB, closedA, closedB>>

TypeOK == /\ votesA \subseteq Controllers
          /\ votesB \subseteq Controllers
          /\ votesA \cap votesB = {}
          /\ closedA \in BOOLEAN
          /\ closedB \in BOOLEAN

Init == /\ votesA = {}
        /\ votesB = {}
        /\ closedA = FALSE
        /\ closedB = FALSE

\* A controller not yet committed to either runway may cast a vote for it.
VoteA(c) == /\ c \notin votesA
            /\ c \notin votesB
            /\ votesA' = votesA \cup {c}
            /\ UNCHANGED <<votesB, closedA, closedB>>

VoteB(c) == /\ c \notin votesA
            /\ c \notin votesB
            /\ votesB' = votesB \cup {c}
            /\ UNCHANGED <<votesA, closedA, closedB>>

CommitA == /\ ~closedA
           /\ Cardinality(votesA) >= Quorum
           /\ closedA' = TRUE
           /\ UNCHANGED <<votesA, votesB, closedB>>

CommitB == /\ ~closedB
           /\ Cardinality(votesB) >= Quorum
           /\ closedB' = TRUE
           /\ UNCHANGED <<votesA, votesB, closedA>>

\* A tick where no controller votes and no closure commits.
Idle == UNCHANGED vars

Next == \/ \E c \in Controllers : VoteA(c) \/ VoteB(c)
        \/ CommitA
        \/ CommitB
        \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(CommitA) /\ WF_vars(CommitB)

QuorumA == Cardinality(votesA) >= Quorum
QuorumB == Cardinality(votesB) >= Quorum

\* A runway is only ever irreversibly closed once its quorum truly was met.
SafetyOnceOnly == (closedA => QuorumA) /\ (closedB => QuorumB)

\* Once a runway's quorum is reached, that runway's closure eventually commits.
EventualCommit == (QuorumA ~> closedA) /\ (QuorumB ~> closedB)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
    Quorum = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SafetyOnceOnly

PROPERTY EventualCommit
nl:
This spec models an air-traffic runway allocator responsible for two independent runway-closure decisions - closing Runway A for resurfacing and closing Runway B for resurfacing - that draw their approving votes from one shared pool of duty controllers. Each controller in the shared pool may cast a single approval vote for whichever runway closure they currently support, but because their attention is a shared, limited resource, a controller who has already voted for one runway's closure cannot also vote for the other's. The action set is: VoteA, in which an available controller (one who has not yet voted for either closure) casts an approval vote for closing Runway A; VoteB, the symmetric action for Runway B; CommitA, which irreversibly commits the decision to close Runway A once its vote tally reaches the required quorum of controllers and it has not already been committed; CommitB, the symmetric irreversible commit for Runway B; and Idle, representing a tick where no controller acts and no commit fires, keeping the allocator responsive even when no vote or commit is currently warranted.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A runway closure is only ever irreversibly committed once its approval-vote tally has actually reached the required quorum, for both Runway A and Runway B.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Once a runway's vote tally reaches the required quorum, that runway's closure is eventually committed.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m2p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* A car-wash conveyor line admits cars via a two-phase-commit handshake
\* between its participants (every participant must "prepare" before a
\* Commit admits the car), except that a privileged admin override can push
\* a car straight onto the conveyor while still respecting bay capacity.

CONSTANTS Participants, Capacity, MaxWaiting

VARIABLES waiting, occupied, phase, votes

vars == <<waiting, occupied, phase, votes>>

TypeOK == /\ waiting \in 0..MaxWaiting
          /\ occupied \in 0..Capacity
          /\ phase \in {"idle", "prepared"}
          /\ votes \subseteq Participants

Init == /\ waiting = 0
        /\ occupied = 0
        /\ phase = "idle"
        /\ votes = {}

CarArrives == /\ waiting < MaxWaiting
              /\ waiting' = waiting + 1
              /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, phase, votes>>

RequestEntry == /\ phase = "idle"
                /\ waiting > 0
                /\ occupied < Capacity
                /\ waiting' = waiting - 1
                /\ phase' = "prepared"
                /\ votes' = {}
                /\ UNCHANGED occupied

Prepare(p) == /\ phase = "prepared"
              /\ p \notin votes
              /\ votes' = votes \cup {p}
              /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, occupied, phase>>

Commit == /\ phase = "prepared"
          /\ votes = Participants
          /\ occupied < Capacity
          /\ occupied' = occupied + 1
          /\ phase' = "idle"
          /\ votes' = {}
          /\ UNCHANGED waiting

Abort == /\ phase = "prepared"
         /\ phase' = "idle"
         /\ votes' = {}
         /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, occupied>>

\* Privileged override: skips the participant vote entirely, but the bay
\* capacity guard still applies exactly as it does for an ordinary Commit.
AdminForceAdmit == /\ occupied < Capacity
                   /\ occupied' = occupied + 1
                   /\ phase' = "idle"
                   /\ votes' = {}
                   /\ UNCHANGED waiting

Exit == /\ occupied > 0
        /\ occupied' = occupied - 1
        /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, phase, votes>>

Next == \/ CarArrives
        \/ RequestEntry
        \/ \E p \in Participants : Prepare(p)
        \/ Commit
        \/ Abort
        \/ AdminForceAdmit
        \/ Exit

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The number of cars on the conveyor never exceeds the fixed bay capacity,
\* whether admitted via the ordinary vote or via the admin's override.
CapacityInvariant == occupied <= Capacity

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Participants = {p1, p2}
    Capacity = 2
    MaxWaiting = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CapacityInvariant
nl:
This spec models a car-wash conveyor line with a bounded number of wash bays. Cars first join a waiting queue outside the line before being admitted onto the conveyor, and admission onto the conveyor is governed by a two-phase-commit handshake between the line's participants (for example, the entry-sensor controller and the wash-station controller), except when the line's privileged admin steps in and forces a car through directly. The action set is: CarArrives, which adds a new car to the outside waiting queue (up to its bounded size); RequestEntry, which - only when the conveyor is not already negotiating an admission and there is bay room free - pulls one car off the waiting queue and opens a two-phase-commit round to admit it; Prepare, in which any one participant records its prepare-phase approval for the currently open admission round; Commit, which - only once every participant has recorded approval and a bay is still free - actually admits the car onto the conveyor and closes the round; Abort, which lets an open admission round be abandoned without admitting a car, returning the line to idle; AdminForceAdmit, the privileged override that lets the admin push a waiting decision through and place a car onto the conveyor immediately, skipping the participant vote entirely, but still only when a bay is free; and Exit, which removes a finished car from the conveyor, freeing a bay. Even though the admin's override bypasses the normal participant negotiation, it is still bound by the same bay-capacity check as ordinary two-phase-commit admissions.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of cars occupying the conveyor's wash bays never exceeds the line's fixed bay capacity, whether cars are admitted through the ordinary two-phase-commit vote or through the admin's override.
